evidence: Plaut. Mil. 4.4.43: palliolum habeās ferrūgineum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Of the colour of iron rust” (ferrūgō), a dark, dusky red (Lewis & Short).

Lewis & Short heads it rōbīg-, with rūbīg- as a variant; classically it means rusty, covered with rust, of things like a strigil or a sword. Traupman lists it among the colours; for the colour the classical word is ferrūgineus.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
